prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: square detailed painterly mythology encyclopedia illustration. Primary request: ONE SAZAKAN, the Turkic and Altai whirlwind storm spirit, choosing the huge dragon-like being with branching horns described in Deniz Karakurt's Türk Söylence Sözlüğü. High above an empty Central Asian mountain wilderness, show one enormous nonhuman dragon head with a long reptilian snout and TWO clearly branching tree-bough-like horns, each horn growing from the back of its skull and splitting into antler-like branches. The long scaled neck and sinuous body sweep in one enormous curve through roiling clouds, lower body visibly transforming into a single descending tornado funnel: a supernatural transformation, not a second creature. Do not invent unseen appendages: this picture depicts a head and continuous serpentlike storm-body emerging from cloud, no visible legs or wings. Exactly one head, two horn roots, one continuous body and one vortex. Branching horns are the signature feature and must be clearly legible. Rain sheets and small pale hailstones whirl around the spirit, lightning illuminates cloud layers above craggy mountain peaks. Elemental wild, powerful, unpredictable and ambivalent storm aura, not a malicious humanoid demon. Refined textured painted realism, storm slate and blue-grey scales with silver lightning highlights, dragon face alert and primal. Whole silhouette and horns fit within frame; atmosphere must preserve visible horns, face, neck and body continuity. Constraints: no humans, ordinary human portrait, clothing, weapons, buildings, extra heads, extra horn roots, extra monsters, text, border or watermark. This is an artistic cloud-body manifestation of the researched branched-horn dragon variant; do not make a fiery dwarf or mix in bird anatomy.
depicted_variant: Huge branching-horn dragon-like storm spirit manifesting from cloud into a whirlwind
visual_requirements: Huge nonhuman dragon-like head and cloud-bound body
Two visibly branched horn roots, one head and continuous body
Single storm vortex with rain, hail and lightning
Mountain-cloud setting and wild unpredictable elemental aura
aura: Wild immense unpredictable elemental storm power; ambivalent rain and hail spirit

additional_sources.title: Deniz Karakurt — Türk Söylence Sözlüğü, 2011, page 179, SAZAKAN
additional_sources.purpose: Direct dictionary passage confirms huge dragon-like being, branching horns, cloud residence, strengthened rain and lightning. Cloud-body depiction is artistic interpretation of transformation to whirlwind; no claim of a specific traditional limb count.

visual_review.notes: Individually inspected with view_image. Observed one clearly nonhuman reptilian head, two major horn roots dividing into many bough-like branches, one scaled neck and curved body emerging from storm cloud and one descending funnel. No visible legs or wings are invented for this cloud-body manifestation; no humans or humanoid portrait. Rain, swirling pale hailstones and forks of lightning over snowy rugged mountain wilderness preserve immense unpredictable elemental storm power. Branching horns remain the dominant identifying feature. Creature is shown in a transformation phase rather than asserting a fixed anatomical limb count.
